title: Telemetry-driven mitigation for sustained prefetch degradation under tenant surges
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent SLA breaches correlated with sustained microburst traffic patterns (~30-90s) of small requests. Root cause analysis points to a prefetch path degeneracy combined with continuous-batcher admission dynamics: aggressive prefetches from the runtime are allocating admission capacity, causing KV cache churn and starving long-context flows such that long-request tail latency (99th/99.9th) spikes by 3-8x. Impact spans Hosted (shared pool), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools under tenant microbursts) and a Private deployment where noisy internal clients reproduced the pattern. This ticket scopes detection, emergency mitigation, and a robust fix that preserves throughput while protecting latency-sensitive flows.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate mixed-length workload with 90% small inference requests (context <= 64) hitting a single tenant for 60s, followed immediately by a set of long-context requests (context >= 4096).
Observe admission window saturation: continuous-batcher composes many small-token batches and prefetch threads enqueue evictions into KV cache.
Trigger telemetry collection: enable runtime debug metrics and trace id for mixed tenant; collect batch composition histogram and KV eviction rate.
Reproduce on Hosted canary (us-east-1) with synthetic load generator (scripts/loadgen/prefetch_surge.py).
diagnostics: Batch composition histogram shows >85% of batches during surge composed solely of small requests; prefetch task count spikes by 12x.
KV cache hit rate collapses from 92% to 36% within 20s of sustained surge.
Admission_token_consumption metric shows prefetch and small-request lanes consuming >95% of admission tokens leading to queue starvation for long flows.
CPU profiler indicates prefetch worker thrash + GC pressure in Dedicated control plane when tenant microburst occurs.
Grafana dashboard: grafana.redwood.com/d/rt/scheduler-long-tail?var=tenant=S-Blue (redacted) shows 99.9th token latency spike aligned with prefetch_eviction counter elevation.
design_decision: Introduce a conservative 'reserve window' that guarantees a configurable fraction of admission capacity for latency-sensitive (long-context) flows, plus tenant-level prefetch concurrency limits and telemetry-driven backoff for prefetch tasks. The reserve window is small by default (2-5% of admission tokens) to avoid throughput regression, and tunable per-deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). This balances fairness with throughput and is reversible via runtime flag for emergency rollbacks.
implementation_notes: Add admission.reserved_tokens metric and gauge in scheduler core; expose via telemetry and per-tenant dimension.
Limit prefetch concurrency via runtime config: prefetch.max_concurrent_per_tenant (default 2).
Implement exponential backoff with jitter for prefetch when prefetch_eviction_rate > threshold (configurable).
Small hotpatch: admission hard-cap for prefetch threads to protect long flows while longer-term reserve window is QA'd (branch hotfix/admission-cap-50301).
Ensure change is gated behind feature-flag and operator-config for Private deployments (operator can set reserve window to 0 during experiments).
Add unit tests for admission accounting and fuzz tests for mixed-length load to ensure no regression in throughput >5% for typical workloads.
acceptance_criteria: 99th/99.9th token latency for long-context requests reduced by at least 50% under the previously failing synthetic surge profile.
No increase >8% in aggregate token throughput for normal mixed workloads after enabling reserve window by default on canary.
New telemetry counters (admission.reserved_tokens, prefetch.eviction_rate, prefetch.active_concurrency) emitted and visible in Grafana.
Post-deploy customer validation: S-Blue confirms SLA breaches no longer reproduced in their Dedicated pool under identical load.
Configuration documented in Confluence and ops runbook updated with rollback steps.
rollout_plan: 1) Push hotpatch (admission-cap) to Hosted canary cluster + monitor for 2 hours.
2) If stable, deploy reserve-window feature-flagged build to us-east-1 canary (hosted) and enable telemetry.
3) Gradually enable reserve window for 5% of Hosted tenant traffic; monitor 99/99.9 tail and throughput metrics for 24h.
4) After canary verification, schedule Dedicated pool deploys during low-traffic maintenance windows; coordinate with Dedicated account owners (S-Blue, AcmeAI).
5) Provide toggle and operator docs for Private customers; offer patch assistance to on-prem customers and include the change in runtime-1.21 release notes.
Rollback: disable reserve-window config or revert hotfix branch if we see >10% throughput regression or unexpected queueing.
github_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2158 -- tests: mixed-length fuzz harness + CI flake guards
qa_checks: Run loadgen profile: scripts/loadgen/mixed_mini_burst.yml against canary clusters and record P50/P95/P99/P99.9 for long and short flows.
Verify new telemetry counters exist and alerts are created for prefetch.eviction_rate > 10% sustained.
Confirm unit and integration tests pass in CI; run fuzz harness for 6k mixed traces without admission violation assertions.
